title: They begged Him… and still refused to bow.
paragraphs: They begged Him… and still refused to bow.
Because this is where many people get exposed.

You can recognize Jesus…
and still resist Him.

You can speak truth…
and still reject surrender.

You can believe He is Lord…
and still live like you are.
But something in this story should disturb you.
Because the ones begging Jesus in Luke 8…
weren’t broken sinners trying to be saved.
And they had something many humans today don’t have—
They knew exactly who Jesus was.

No confusion.
No hesitation.
No debate.
What if someone today is doing the same?
Because this is not just a Bible story.
The man in Luke 8 was extreme.

Chains couldn’t hold him.
Society rejected him.
He lived among the dead.

We sit in church with clean clothes
and unclean hearts.

We post verses online
but hide secret sins offline.

We say “God knows my heart”
while refusing to let Him change it.
You can be close to Jesus… and still not be free.
The demons were in the presence of Jesus.

Closer than the crowds.
Closer than the disciples at that moment.

You can attend every service.
Listen to every sermon.
Even feel something emotional during worship.
Because deception doesn’t always look dark.
Some people don’t reject Jesus openly.
Demons never struggled with identity confusion about Jesus.
“What have You to do with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God?” (Luke 8:28)
Let’s anchor this in the Word.

“And they begged Him not to command them to depart into the abyss.”
— Luke 8:31
And that’s where many people are today.

“You believe that God is one; you do well. Even the demons believe—and shudder!”
— James 2:19
Some scholars interpret this as a warning that intellectual belief without a transformed life reveals a dead faith—one that acknowledges truth but refuses submission.
Because the story doesn’t end with demons.
becomes the man who is restored.

“Then people went out to see what had happened… and found the man… sitting at the feet of Jesus, clothed and in his right mind.”
— Luke 8:35
Jesus didn’t negotiate with the demons.
Not just to deal with demons—
but to deal with your sin.
Because the real enemy is not just external.

Pride.
Lust.
Hidden bitterness.
Unforgiveness.
Self-rule.
Sin is not just what you do.
It’s what separates you from God.

“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.”
— Romans 3:23

“But God shows His love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.”
— Romans 5:8
Jesus didn’t wait for you to fix yourself.
So you don’t have to beg like demons…
You can be saved like the man.
But salvation requires something demons will never do—

“Repent therefore, and turn back, that your sins may be blotted out.”
— Acts 3:19
Repentance is not just feeling bad.
Or are you surrendering to Him?
You don’t have to stay chained.
You don’t have to stay divided.
You don’t have to live in hidden compromise.
But He will not force you.
“I don’t just want to believe… I want to follow.”
Because no chain outranks His authority.
